name_story.story: Zubaidah can be understood through the Arabic form زُبَيْدَة, whose central sense is zubaidah; diminutive of zubda, cream (feminine) (malay form). Zubaidah is the Malay form of Arabic زُبَيْدَة (Zubayda), the diminutive of زُبْدَة, meaning 'cream'.

faq.a: Zubaidah is associated with the Arabic form زُبَيْدَة, whose core sense is zubaidah; diminutive of zubda, cream (feminine) (malay form).

faq.q: What is the origin of Zubaidah?
faq.a: Zubaidah is associated with Arabic. Zubaidah is the Malay form of Arabic زُبَيْدَة (Zubayda), the diminutive of زُبْدَة, meaning 'cream'.
Yes — the underlying form زُبَيْدَة is Arabic.
Zubaidah can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Zubaidah should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Zubayda is not a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Zubaidah mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Zubaidah is rendered زبیدہ and carries the sense زبیدہ، مکھن.

faq.q: What does Zubaidah mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Zubaidah is rendered زبیده and carries the sense زبیده، سرشیر.
A romanized syllable approximation is zu-bai-dah. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Zubaidah?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Zubaidah, zubaidah. Script forms are زبيده, زبیده, زبیدہ, زُبَيْدَة, ज़ुबैदा.

faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
